translations.reference: A study published on Thursday in the journal Science reported on formation of a new bird species on the Ecuadorean Galápagos Islands.
translations.hypothesis: A recent study published in the scientific journal "Nature" details a new species of finch discovered on the Ecuadorian Galapagos Islands.

translations.source: Àwọn aṣèwádìí láti ilé ẹ̀kọ́ gíga Princeton ní United States àti Ilé ẹ̀ka gíga Uppsala ní sweden jábọ̀ ìròyìn ẹ̀yà tuntun ní ó wà ní ìran méjì, ṣùgbọ́n ètò yìí ma ń gba àkókò, látàrí dídàgbà láàrín endemic Darwin finch, Geospiza forted, àti ìṣílọ cactus finch, Geospiza conirostris.
translations.reference: Researchers from Princeton University in the United States and Uppsala University in Sweden reported the new species evolved in just two generations, though this process had been believed to take much longer, due to breeding between an endemic Darwin finch, Geospiza fortes, and the immigrant cactus finch, Geospiza conirostris.
translations.hypothesis: Researchers from Princeton University in the United States and Uppsala University in Sweden have announced the discovery of a new species of bird. However, the species is endangered, due to competition with the endemic Darwin's finch, *Geospiza fording*, and the cactus finch, *Geospiza conirostris*.

translations.source: A lè kan wúra sí àpere púpọ̀, a lè yíi sí àpere kékèké.
translations.reference: Gold may be worked into all sorts of shapes. It can be rolled into tiny shapes.
translations.hypothesis: We can write a message on a large piece of paper, or we can write it on a small piece of paper.

translations.source: Wọ́n lè fàá sínu wáyà tó tínrín, tí a lè yí tí a tún lè dì a lè gbá ǹkan le lórí tàbí kí a we sínu aṣọ.
translations.reference: It can be pulled into thin wire, which can be twisted and plaited. It can be hammered or rolled into sheets.
translations.hypothesis: It can be folded into a small, compact shape, making it easy to store or carry, and it can also be used as a cushion or placed inside a garment.

translations.source: O ṣeeṣe ni tinrin, ti a o si fi bo irin miran. o si ṣeeṣe ni ọna ti o jẹ wipe yio ṣe lo lati fi ṣe ẹṣo si awon aworan alafowoya ninu awọn iwe ti a n pe ni “Illuminated manuscript.”
translations.reference: It can be made very thin, and stuck onto other metal. It can be made so thin that it was sometimes used to decorate the hand-painted pictures in books called "illuminated manuscripts".
translations.hypothesis: It is indeed a beautiful thing, and it is also a technique that was used to add embellishments to the illustrations in books known as "illuminated manuscripts."

translations.source: Eléyìí ni à ń pè ní pH apòògùn. O lè se asàmì pẹ̀lú lílo ohun ẹlẹ́rìndòdò pupa ti kábèjì.
translations.reference: This is called a chemical's pH. You can make an indicator using red cabbage juice.
translations.hypothesis: This is what we call the "pharmaceutical pH." It can be determined using a universal indicator solution.

translations.source: Omi kabeeji maa paro awo eyi dalelori oye asidi tabi besiki (alkalaini) to wa ninu kemika naa.
translations.reference: The cabbage juice changes color depending on how acidic or basic (alkaline) the chemical is.
translations.hypothesis: The water will react with the acid or base (alkaline substance) present in the chemical.

translations.source: Átọka ìwọ̀n áásìdì sàfihàn nípasè iyẹ Hydrogen ( H nínú pH) mólẹ́kù nínú kẹ́míkàli tí a sẹ àyẹ̀wò rẹ.
translations.reference: The pH level is indicated by the amount of Hydrogen (the H in pH) ions in the tested chemical.
translations.hypothesis: The basic principle of pH measurement is based on the concentration of hydrogen ions (H+) in a chemical solution being analyzed.

translations.source: Hydrogen ions jẹ́ protons tó ní electron tí wọ́n bọ́ lára wọn (nítoríHydrogen atoms ní proton kan àti electron kan).
translations.reference: Hydrogen ions are protons that had their electrons stripped off them (since Hydrogen atoms consist of one proton and one electron).
translations.hypothesis: Hydrogen ions are protons that have lost an electron (because hydrogen atoms have one proton and one electron).

translations.source: Po àwọn eruku gbígbẹ̀ méjì pọ̀ kí o wa mún ọ̀wọ́ tútù tó mọ́ fi fún wọn pọ̀ di bọ́ọ̀lù.
translations.reference: Swirl the two dry powders together and then, with clean wet hands, squeeze them into a ball.
translations.hypothesis: After the two dogs got together, they found a smooth, round object that they decided to play with like a ball.

translations.source: Ọ̀rinrin ọwọ́ rẹ yíò dáhùn kíákíá sì ìpele tó wà níta, èyí tí yíò rí bákan tàbí se àkójọ ìkaraun.
translations.reference: The moisture on your hands will react with the outer layers, which will feel funny and form a sort of shell.
translations.hypothesis: The sound of your music will bring great joy to the audience, whether it's a live performance or a recorded piece.

translations.source: Àwọn ìlú Harappa àti Mohenjo-daro fẹẹrẹ ní ilé ìgbònsẹ̀ oní kọ̀lọ̀fìn omi ní gbogbo ilé, ti o so mọ ìlànà kógbè-kógbè ẹlẹgẹ́.
translations.reference: The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had a flush toilet in almost every house, attached to a sophisticated sewage system.
translations.hypothesis: The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro featured sophisticated drainage systems throughout the city, which were connected to a central sewage system.

translations.source: A ti rí ṣálángá tó ṣẹkù nínú àwọn ilé ní agbègbè Minoan ti Crete àti Santorini ní Greece.
translations.reference: Remains of sewage systems have been found in the houses of the Minoan cities of Crete and Santorini in Greece.
translations.hypothesis: Fragments of clay tablets have been discovered in homes in the Minoan regions of Crete and Santorini in Greece.

translations.source: Ile igbonse wa ni Ijipti, Pesia ati Saina atijo. Ni Roomu, ile igbonse maa n saba wa lara ibi iwe gbogboogbo ni ibi ti okunrin ati obinrin ma n jo wapo.
translations.reference: There were also toilets in ancient Egypt, Persia and China. In Roman civilization, toilets were sometimes part of public bath houses where men and women were together in mixed company.
translations.hypothesis: Our company has operations in Egypt, Persia, and ancient China. In Rome, bathhouses were a common feature of public spaces, where men and women would gather and socialize.

translations.source: Ti o ba pe eniti o jina si o pelu egberun maili, ero ayelujara lo n lo.
translations.reference: When you call someone who is thousands of miles away, you are using a satellite.
translations.hypothesis: If you call someone who is miles away, the internet is being used.

translations.source: Sátálàìtì tó wà nínú òfúrufú ń gba ìpè ó sì tún sàfihàn rẹ̀ pádà sílẹ̀ lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀.
translations.reference: The satellite in space gets the call and then reflects it back down, almost instantly.
translations.hypothesis: The dust that had accumulated began to settle, and the air gradually cleared.

translations.source: Wọ́n ran satalaiti ló sí spéèsì pẹ̀lú rokeeti. Àwọn onimo sayensi ma n lo teliskoopi ni sleesi nitori pe afẹ́fẹ́ ma n kóba ina wa ati nkan to ba ri.
translations.reference: The satellite was sent into space by a rocket. Scientists use telescopes in space because the Earth’s atmosphere distorts some of our light and view.
translations.hypothesis: They launched a satellite into space using a rocket. Scientists often use telescopes in space because the Earth's atmosphere can distort light and obscure objects.

translations.source: O pẹ fún rọkẹtì nla tó ga jù ìwọ̀n ẹsẹ́ ọgọ́rùn kan lọ láti gbẹ satelaiti tábì àwọn ẹ̀rọ́ ìwòyẹ sínú òfuruufú.
translations.reference: It takes a giant rocket over a 100 feet high to put a satellite or telescope in space.
translations.hypothesis: A large rocket, taller than a ten-story building, is used to launch satellites or other equipment into space.

translations.source: Wíìlì ti yí àyé padà ní ọ̀nà púpọ̀. Nkan tó tóbi jùlọ tí wíìlì ṣe fún wa ni pé o mú ìrìn àjò yá àti rọrùn fún wa.
translations.reference: The wheel has changed the world in incredible ways. The biggest thing that the wheel has done for us is given us much easier and faster transportation.
translations.hypothesis: Wheels have revolutionized the way we live. The most significant contribution of wheels is that they have made transportation easier and more efficient.

translations.source: Ó ti mún ọkọ̀ ojú irin, ọkọ̀ ilẹ̀ àtàwọn ohun èlò ìrìnnà míràn wá.
translations.reference: It has brought us the train, the car, and many other transportation devices.
translations.hypothesis: A car, along with other household appliances, arrived.

translations.source: Àwọn olóógbò kéèké tó má ń jẹ àwọn àpajẹ kéèkèé bẹ̀rẹ̀ láti orí ehiri lọ sí ìgalà àti àgbọ̀nrín.
translations.reference: Under them are more medium sized cats that eat medium sized prey ranging from rabbits to antelopes and deer.
translations.hypothesis: Small children who are prone to tantrums often exhibit these behaviors from the head down to the feet and abdomen.

translations.source: NÍgbẹ̀yìn, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn olóógbò kéèké (nínú èyí tí olóógbó igbó wà) ó má ń jẹ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àpajẹ bíi kòkòrò, èkúté, aláǹgbá àti ẹyẹ.
translations.reference: Finally, there are many small cats (including loose pet cats) that eat the far more numerous small prey like insects, rodents, lizards, and birds.
translations.hypothesis: In general, many small animals (including forest animals) consume a variety of foods such as insects, snails, slugs, and worms.

translations.source: Àṣírí àṣeyọrí wọn ní ìmọ̀ nípa níṣì, iṣẹ́ àkànṣe tí ológbò kookan lè ṣe láyì díje pẹ̀lú àwọn míì.
translations.reference: The secret to their success is the concept of the niche, a special job each cat holds that keeps it from competing with others.
translations.hypothesis: Their success stems from their knowledge of the subject matter and the ability of each student to work effectively with others.

translations.source: Kìnìún ni ẹranko ológbò tó lajú jù, tí o máa n wà ní agbo ńlá tí a sì máa ń pè ní olólà ijù.
translations.reference: Lions are the most social cats, living in large groups called prides.
translations.hypothesis: The rhinoceros is a large, herbivorous mammal that is found in grasslands and is also known as the "horn-bearing beast."

translations.source: Àkójọpọ̀ kínìú jẹ́ akọ métà, pẹ̀lú ọgbọ̀n abo àti àwọn ọmọ wọn.
translations.reference: Prides are made up of one to three related adult males, along with as many as thirty females and cubs.
translations.hypothesis: The family consisted of three people: a couple and their child.

translations.source: Àwọn obìnrin wọn ma ń súma ara wọn, nítorí wọ́n jẹ́ ẹbí tó tóbi tóní àwọn ọmọ obìnri.
translations.reference: The females are usually closely related to each other, being a large family of sisters and daughters.
translations.hypothesis: Women often feel pressured because they are expected to be the primary caregivers for their children.

translations.source: Àwọn àkópọ̀ kìnìhún máà wùwà bí àpẹ́jọpọ̀ ìkookò tàbí ajá, ìyanilẹ́nu ló jẹ́ wípẹ́ awon ẹranko bi kìnìhún (àmọ́ tí kì í se àwọn olóńgbò tó tóbi) ní ìhùwàsí, pẹ̀lú pé wọ́n léwu fún àwọn ẹranko ìjẹ..
translations.reference: Lion prides act much like packs of wolves or dogs, animals surprisingly similar to lions (but not other big cats) in behavior, and also very deadly to their prey.
translations.hypothesis: Antelopes are often mistaken for deer or goats. However, antelopes (which are not closely related to deer) are generally smaller in size, and they have horns, while deer do not. Furthermore, antelopes are herbivores.

translations.source: Eléré ìje tó dá ń tọ́, ẹkùn lè gùn ún (ó lè má tọ̀ọ́ dáadáa)lúwẹ̀ẹ́, fo ibi tó jínna, bẹ́ẹ̀ ló lè fa ohun tí èèyàn tó sángun lè fà fún ìgbà márùn ún.
translations.reference: A well rounded athlete, the tiger can climb (though not well), swim, leap great distances and pull with five times the force of a strong human.
translations.hypothesis: If a race is too competitive, a runner might get injured (or it might not be ideal), they might get discouraged, and it could lead to them giving up running altogether.

translations.source: Ẹkùn náà wà nínu ẹgbk kanáà (Genus Panthera) gẹ́gk bí kìnìú, àmọ̀tékù, àti olóngbò ńlá. Àwọn olọ́ngbò mẹrin wọ̀nyí nìkan ló lè dún.
translations.reference: The tiger is in the same group (Genus Panthera) as lions, leopards, and jaguars. These four cats are the only ones who can roar.
translations.hypothesis: This animal belongs to the cat family (Genus Panthera), which includes lions, tigers, and leopards. These four species are the only ones that can roar.

translations.source: Kikun ekun ko dabi ti kinikun to kun, sugbon o dabi gbolohun aso, oro onigbe.
translations.reference: The tiger's roar is not like the full-voiced roar of a lion, but more like a sentence of snarly, shouted words.
translations.hypothesis: The sound of the snake's hiss is not like the sound of a snake shedding its skin, but rather like the rustling of fabric or the whisper of a secret.

translations.source: Àwọn olóńgbò jẹranjẹran féràn láti ma jẹ ẹranko kekeke. Wọn a mú àwọn ọ̀bọ, ejò, ẹ̀kútẹ́ àti ẹyẹ tí ọwọ́ wọn bá tẹ̀. Bí i gbogbo ẹranko ti olóńgbo jẹranjẹran fi n ṣe ọdẹ rẹ ni o kẹ́rẹ́ juu lọ.
translations.reference: Ocelots like to eat small animals. They will catch monkeys, snakes, rodents and birds if they can. Almost all of the animals that the ocelot hunts are far smaller than it is.
translations.hypothesis: Farmers often cultivate small plots of land. They plant crops like vegetables, herbs, and fruits, depending on what they can grow with their available resources. The yield from these small farms is typically higher than that of larger, more commercial farms.

translations.source: Àwọn onímọ̀ sáyẹnsì gbàgbọ́ pé àwọn Osiloti ma ń fí oorun wá àti tẹ̀lé eranko tí wọn fẹ́ jẹ.
translations.reference: Scientists think that ocelots follow and find animals to eat (prey) by smell, sniffing for where they've been on the ground.
translations.hypothesis: Scientists believe that ostriches often bask in the sun and roll in the sand.

translations.source: Wọ́n ríran dada ní òkùnkùn pẹ̀lú iràn òkùnkùn àti pe wọn ma n yọ́ rìn náà. Àwọn Osiloti ma n pa àwọ̀ da láti bá àyíká rẹ̀ rẹ́ kó ba lè bà léàwọn eranko tí wọ́n ma jẹ.
translations.reference: They can see very well in the dark with night vision, and move very stealthily, too. Ocelots hunt their prey by blending in with their surroundings then pouncing on their prey.
translations.hypothesis: They are often found in dark, secluded places, and they tend to move quickly. Snakes are sometimes kept as pets, but they require specialized care and can be dangerous if not handled properly.

translations.source: Nígbà tí ẹgbẹ́ kékeré nǹkan abẹ̀mí (tó kéré níye) bá yẹra kúrò lọ́dọ̀ àwọn olùgbé àkọ́kọ́ tíwọ́n ti wá (bí i kí wọ́n kúrò lórí òkè àbí odò tàbí tí wọ́n bá kó lọ sí erékùsù tuntun kí wọ́n má lè padà mọ́) wọ́n yíò ri wípé wọ́n bára wọn ní àyíká tó yàtọ̀ ju ibi tí wọ́n wà tẹ́lẹ̀ lọ.
translations.reference: When a small group of living things (a small population) gets separated from the main population that they came from (like if they move over a mountain range or a river, or if they move to a new island so that they can't easily move back) they will often find themselves in a different environment than they were in before.
translations.hypothesis: When a small group of animals (that are young) separate from the main group they came with (whether they leave the herd, flock, or school, or move to a new location), they will find themselves in a situation that is different from what they are used to.

translations.source: Agbègbè tuntun ní ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ohun àlùmọ́nì àti àwọn orogún òwò lóríṣìíríṣìí, fún ìdí èyí iye ènìyàn tuntun yóò nílò oríṣìíríṣìí nǹkan láti ní okun tí wọ́n fi lè kọjú àwọn tí wọ́n jọ ń sorogún.
translations.reference: This new environment has different resources and different competitors, so the new population will need different features or adaptations to be a strong competitor than what they had needed before.
translations.hypothesis: The new area has many opportunities and various challenges, which means that new residents will need a variety of resources to integrate and thrive within the community.

translations.source: Ojúlówó iye kò yípadà rárá, wọ́n túbọ̀ nílò láti ṣe àmúlò ẹ̀da bíí ti àtijọ́.
translations.reference: The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before.
translations.hypothesis: The cost of living has not decreased significantly, and there is still a great need to create more jobs, as in the past.

translations.source: Bí àkókò ṣe ń lọ, bí àwọn olùgbé titun ṣe n yípadà sí àyíká wọn, wọn ò ní fibẹ́ẹ̀ jọ àwọn olùgbé tókù.
translations.reference: Over time, as the new population begins to adapt to their new environment, they start to look less and less like the other population.
translations.hypothesis: As time passes and new students join the school, they will not be able to sit together with the older students.

translations.source: Láìpẹ́, léyìn egberun tàbi mílíọ́nù ọdún, iye àwọn èèyàn náà ò ní jọra tó jẹ́ pé a ò lè pe wọ́n ní ęgbẹ́ alàyè kán náà.
translations.reference: Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the two populations will look so different that they can't be called the same species.
translations.hypothesis: Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the number of those people would not be so great that we could no longer consider them a distinct group.

translations.source: A pè ìṣètò yìí ní ẹ̀yà, èyí tó túms sí pé ẹ̀yà tuntun. Ẹ̀yà jẹ́ àtubọ̀tán tí a kò lè yẹra fún ó sì jẹ́ ǹkan pàtàkì fún ìtànkálẹ̀.
translations.reference: We call this process speciation, which just means the formation of new species. Speciation is an unavoidable consequence and a very important part of evolution.
translations.hypothesis: This feature is called "innovation," which implies a new and original idea. Innovation is a process that cannot be rushed and is crucial for progress.

translations.source: Awon ewe lo n se eemi ti awon omo eyan maa n mi sinu, won si ma n gba eemi ti awon eyan ma n mi si ta (eyi to je, .
translations.reference: Plants make oxygen which humans breathe, and they take in carbon-dioxide which humans exhale (that is, breathe out).
translations.hypothesis: Plants absorb the carbon dioxide that humans exhale, and they also absorb the carbon dioxide that humans produce through activities like burning fuel (e.g., driving cars).

translations.source: Fotosintesisi ni ọ̀nà tí àwọn ewé ma n gbà gi ṣe ounje wọn láti orun. Wọ́n dẹ̀ ma n pèsè àbò.
translations.reference: Plants make their food from the sun by photosynthesis. They also provide shade.
translations.hypothesis: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight into food. They also release oxygen.

translations.source: A kọ́ àwọn ilé wa pẹ̀lú ewé a sì ṣe àwọn aṣọ wá nínu ewé náà. Púpọ̀ nínú àwọn óúnjẹ́ tí à ń jẹ jẹ́ ewé. Láìsí ewé, àwọn ẹranko kò lè yè.
translations.reference: We make our houses from plants and make clothes from plants. Most foods that we eat are plants. Without plants, animals could not survive.
translations.hypothesis: We build our houses with wood, and we make our clothes from it. Many of the foods we eat are derived from plants. Without plants, animals cannot survive.

translations.source: Mosasaurus je apanirun ti o le ju nigba aye re, ko beru nkankan leyin awon mosasaurs miran.
translations.reference: Mosasaurus was the apex predator of its time, so it feared nothing, except other mosasaurs.
translations.hypothesis: The Mosasaurus was a formidable predator in its time, surpassing all other mosasaurs in size and power.

translations.source: Erigi re to gun kun fun ju 70 eyin to mu, pelu imin ni aja enu re, o tumo si wipe nkan kikan to ba baa pade o le lo lai farapa.
translations.reference: Its long jaws were studded with more than 70 razor-sharp teeth, along with an extra set in the roof of its mouth, meaning that there was no escape for anything that crossed its path.
translations.hypothesis: Standing over 70 inches tall, with a long neck and slender limbs, it appears that nothing can stop this creature.

translations.source: Kòdánilójú, sùgbọ̀n ó lè ti ní ahọ́n amúga. Lára oúnjẹ rẹ̀ ni ìjàpà, ẹja ńlá, àwọn mosasaurs àti pé ó lè jẹ́ àwọn ẹranko tó ń jẹ́ ènìyàn.
translations.reference: We don't know for sure, but it may have had a forked tongue. Its diet included turtles, large fish, other mosasaurs, and it may even have been a cannibal.
translations.hypothesis: Interestingly, it might have had a unique diet. Its diet likely included fish, large animals, and possibly even humans.

translations.source: Ó tún ma ń se àkọlù sí ohunkóhun tó bá wọnú omi; kódà bó jẹ́ dínósọ̀ bí i bí i T. rex kò sì lè kápá rẹ̀.
translations.reference: It also attacked anything that entered the water; even a giant dinosaur such as T. rex would be no match for it.
translations.hypothesis: It also reacts to anything that comes into contact with water; even a creature as large as a T. rex couldn't escape it.

translations.source: Níwọ̀n ìgbà ti àwọn oúnjẹ wọn kò sàjòjì sí wa, àwọnn arà Romu náà ní àwọn àsè tó sàjòjì tàbí tí kò wọ́pọ̀, bi akọ ẹlẹ́dẹ̀, àkùkọ, ìgbín, àti ẹ̀dà eku tí a ń pè ní dormouse.
translations.reference: While most of their food would be familiar to us, Romans did have their share of strange or unusual feast items, including wild boar, peacock, snails, and a type of rodent called a dormouse
translations.hypothesis: During times when food was scarce, the Roman people relied on readily available or easily obtainable resources, such as grains, legumes, nuts, and a type of rodent called a dormouse.

translations.source: Ìyàtọ́ míràn nipé nígbàtí àwọn aláìní àtawọn obìnrin bá ń jẹun tiwọn lórí ìjókòó, àwọn olówó ma ń nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí àsè àpapọ̀ níbití wọn ó ti rọ̀gbọ̀kún lẹ́gbẹ̀ẹ́ méjìjì bí wọ́n bá se ń jẹun.
translations.reference: Another difference was that while the poor people and the woman ate their food while sitting in chairs, the rich men liked to have banquets together where they would lounge on their sides while they ate their meals.
translations.hypothesis: Another difference is that when women are eating together, they often prefer to sit facing each other, especially when they are sharing a meal.

translations.source: Àwọn ounje tó wá sí ile Yuropi láti Amerika àbí Asia ní senturi tó gbẹ̀yìn, o lè wà lára oúnjẹ́ ayé àtijọ́ Romu ò lè.
translations.reference: Ancient Roman meals couldn't have included foods that came to Europe from America or from Asia in later centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The foods that arrived in Europe from America or Asia have a much stronger flavor profile than those found in traditional Roman cuisine.

translations.source: Fún àpẹrẹ wọn ò ní àgbàdo, tomato, ànàmọ́, kòkó, kò dẹ̀ sí ará Roomu àtijọ́ kan kan tó tọ́ pẹ́pẹ́yẹ wò rí.
translations.reference: For instance, they didn't have corn, nor tomatoes, nor potatoes, nor cocoa, and no ancient Roman ever tasted a turkey.
translations.hypothesis: For example, they didn't have any vegetables like beans, tomatoes, or peppers, and there wasn't even a single traditional Roman dish that was properly prepared.

translations.source: Awon ara Bailoni ko tempili gbendeke fun awon orisa kookan won ti won ri gege bi ibugbe orisa naa.
translations.reference: The Babylonians built each of their gods a primary temple that was considered the home of the god.
translations.hypothesis: The people of Baloni built shrines dedicated to each of the deities they worshipped, often locating them near the deity's dwelling place.

translations.source: Àwọn èèyàn yíò mún ẹbọ wá fún òrìṣà àwọn àlúfà yí ó sì gbìyànjú à ti bá àìní àwọn ọlọ́run pàdé látara ayẹyẹ àti ọdún.
translations.reference: People would bring sacrifices to the gods and the priests would try to attend to the needs of the gods through ceremonies and festivals.
translations.hypothesis: These people would offer sacrifices to the ancestral deities and celebrate the connection they felt with the divine, marking important events and seasons.

translations.source: Tẹ́m̀pìlì kọ̀ọ̀kan ló ní ojúde àgbàlà tẹ́ḿpìlì àti inú ibi ìyàsímímọ́ tí àlùfa nìkan lè wọ̀.
translations.reference: Each temple had an open temple courtyard and then an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter.
translations.hypothesis: Each temple has its own sacred space and inner sanctum where only the priest can enter.

translations.source: Nígbà míràn àwọn ilé ìṣọ́ pyramid, tí à ń pè ní ziggurats, ní wọ́n kọ́ láti jẹ́ ara ilé àdúrà.
translations.reference: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples.
translations.hypothesis: In some cases, the pyramid-shaped structures, known as ziggurats, were built as temple complexes.

translations.source: Oke tente ile naa je ibi ijosin pataki fun olorun.
translations.reference: The top of the tower was special sanctuary for the god.
translations.hypothesis: The temple is a sacred place for the deity.

translations.source: Nínú ojú ọjọ́ tó gbóná ti Middle East, ilé náà kò se pàtàkì.
translations.reference: In the warm climate of the Middle East, the house was not so important.
translations.hypothesis: In the context of the broader Middle East, that particular country is not particularly significant.

translations.source: Púpọ̀ nínu ayé àwọn ẹbí Ibru ṣẹlẹ̀ ní afẹ́fẹ́ ìta.
translations.reference: Most of the life of the Hebrew family happened in the open air.
translations.hypothesis: Many events in the Ibru family's life took place outdoors.

translations.source: Àwọn obìrin ló n s’oúnjẹ ní ọgbà, Àwọn ṣọ́bù kàn jẹ́ igbá lásán tón ranjú wo títí. Òkúta ní wọ́n fi ń kọ́ ilé.
translations.reference: Women did the cooking in the yard; stores were just open counters looking into the street. Stone was used for building houses.
translations.hypothesis: The women were cooking in the kitchen, and the children were playing outside, watching them intently. They were using a pot to cook the food.

translations.source: Ko fi be si igbo to tobi ni ile Canaan, nitori naa igi won gan.
translations.reference: There were no large forests in the land of Canaan, so wood was extremely expensive.
translations.hypothesis: They planted the seeds in a large field in the land of Canaan, and the trees grew abundantly.

translations.source: A tẹdo agbegbe Greenland gẹgẹ bi ilu kereje. Ninu iṣẹlẹ Norse, wọn so wipe wọn le Erik Alawo Pupa kuro ni Iceland fun esun ipaniyan, nigbati o n rin irin ajo siwaju si ọna iwo oorun, o ri agbegbe Greenland o si sọ lorukọ.
translations.reference: Greenland was settled sparsely. In the Norse sagas they say that Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for murder, and when travelling further west, found Greenland and named it Greenland.
translations.hypothesis: The discovery of Greenland is often attributed to the Norse. According to Norse sagas, they say that Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for manslaughter. While sailing westward, he encountered the landmass that is now Greenland and named it.

translations.source: Sùgbọ́n láì nání àwárí rẹ̀, ẹ̀yà Eskimo ti ń gbébẹ̀ nígbà náà.
translations.reference: But regardless of his discovery, Eskimo tribes were already living there at the time.
translations.hypothesis: However, despite this, the Eskimo people of that time were still living in the area.

translations.source: Bí ó tilẹ̀jẹ́ wípé ìlú kọ̀kan jẹ́ ará 'Scandinavian', ìyàtọ̀ púpọ̀ wà láàrín àwọn èèyàn, ọba, àṣà,ìṣe àti ìtàn àwn ìlú Denmark, Sweden, Norway àti Iceland.
translations.reference: Though each country was 'Scandinavian', there were many differences between the people, kings, customs and history of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Iceland.
translations.hypothesis: While it might be tempting to categorize each city as "Scandinavian," there are distinct differences in the people, rulers, customs, activities, and history of the cities in Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Iceland.

translations.source: Bí o bá ti wo èré àgbéléwò National Treasure, wà á rò wípé àtọ́ka wúra wà ní kíkọ lẹ́yin ìkéde òmìnira ni.
translations.reference: If you have watched the movie National Treasure, you may think a treasure map was written on the back of the Declaration of Independence.
translations.hypothesis: If you've seen the movie "National Treasure," you might think that clues to hidden treasures are often found in historical documents.

translations.source: Àmọ́ṣá, èyí kò tọ̀nà. lóòótọ́ ohùn kan wà tí wọ́n kọ sí ẹ̀yìn àkọọ́lẹ̀, kìíse ìtọ́nisọ́nà wúra.
translations.reference: However, that is not true. Although there is something written on the back of the document, it is not a treasure map.
translations.hypothesis: Unfortunately, that's not correct. There seems to be a misunderstanding, and it's not about water scarcity.

translations.source: Oro ti ako si eyin Ikede Ominira ni “Ojulowo Ikede ti Ominira eyi ti a se ni 4th July 1776”. Oro naa han ni isale iwe naa, ni adorikodo.
translations.reference: Written on the back of the Declaration of Independence were the words "Original Declaration of Independence dated 4th July 1776". The text appears on the bottom of the document, upside down.
translations.hypothesis: The title of the Declaration of Independence is "The Declaration of Independence, proclaimed on July 4, 1776." The title is located at the bottom of the page, in bold text.

translations.source: Nígbàtí kò sí ẹni tí ó mọ pàtó ẹni tí ó kọ ọ́, ohun tí a mọ̀ ni pé ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ pẹ̀pẹ̀ ayé rẹ̀, ìwé àkọọ́lẹ̀ aláwọ ẹran tí ó tóbi (ó wọn tó 29¾ inṣi sí 24½ inṣì) ní wọ́n yí pamọ́.
translations.reference: While no one knows for certain who wrote it, it is known that early in its life, the large parchment document (it measures 29¾ inches by 24½ inches) was rolled up for storage.
translations.hypothesis: When no one knew the exact identity of the person who owned it, it was revealed that, at the beginning of their life, a large suitcase (measuring approximately 29¾ inches by 24½ inches) was with them.

translations.source: Torina o seese pe won fi akosile naa se lebeeli lasan.
translations.reference: So, it is likely that the notation was added simply as a label.
translations.hypothesis: The investigation revealed that the incident was purely accidental.

translations.source: Ìfibalè ọjọ́ nla náà àti àwọn ogun tó tèle e lọ fún apá Àríwá ìlú Faransé ní òmìnira, súgbọn apá Gúúsù ò tìí di òmìnira.
translations.reference: The D-Day landings and the following battles had freed the north of France, but the south still wasn't free.
translations.hypothesis: The major battles and subsequent events that followed led to the liberation of the northern part of France, but the southern part did not achieve liberation.

translations.source: “Vichy” French ló ṣe adarí rẹ̀. Àwọn ará French niwọ́n tó fẹ́ àláfíà pẹ̀lú àwọn ará ìlú Germany ní 1940 tí wọ́n sì ṣiṣẹ́ pẹ̀lú àwọn tó wá dabẹ̀ rú tí wọ́n kò pè dípò kí wọ́n bá wọn jà lọ.
translations.reference: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.
translations.hypothesis: "Vichy" was a French regime. The French people, who desired peace with the German city dwellers in 1940, collaborated with those who had already surrendered, and they did not hesitate to persecute those who opposed them.

translations.source: Ní ọjọ́ karùndínlógún oṣù kẹjọ ọdún 1940, Àwọn tó jẹ́ ọ̀rẹ́ wọnú ìlú southern France, wọ́n sí pé ìkọlù náà ní “Operation Dragon”.
translations.reference: On 15 August 1940, the Allies invaded southern France, the invasion was called "Operation Dragoon".
translations.hypothesis: On the 22nd of August, 1940, the residents of the southern French town were informed that the operation was codenamed "Operation Dragon."

translations.source: Ní ọ̀sẹ̀ méjì péré ikọ̀ ológun ilẹ̀ Americans àti Free France ti dóòlà ẹkùn gúúsù ilẹ̀ France, wọ́n sì ń padà sí ilẹ̀ Germany.
translations.reference: In just two weeks the Americans and Free French forces had liberated southern France and were turning towards Germany.
translations.hypothesis: Over the course of two weeks, American and Free French forces advanced through northern France and continued their push towards Germany.

translations.source: Ọ̀làjú jẹ́ àṣà tí a pín nípasẹ̀ ẹgbẹ́ tó tóbi tí wọ́n ṣiṣẹ́ tí wọ́n sì ń gbé papọ̀, ẹgbẹ́ kan.
translations.reference: A civilization is a singular culture shared by a significant large group of people who live and work co-operatively, a society.
translations.hypothesis: Olapoju is a tradition that is passed down through a large group of people who work together and live together as a community.

translations.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí à ń pè ní ọ̀làjú wá látí inú èdè ìlú Latin, èyí tó túmọ̀ sí ọ̀làjú ilẹ̀ Latin, civitas túmọ̀ sí ìlú tàbí ìpínlẹp àti pé wọ́n tún fi í se àlàyé bí àwùjọ se tóbi tó.
translations.reference: The word civilization comes from the Latin civilis, meaning civil, related to the Latin civis, meaning citizen, and civitas, meaning city or city-state, and that also somehow defines the size of the society.
translations.hypothesis: The word "city," which comes from the Latin language, translates to "city of Latin," where "city" refers to a town or state, and it is also used to describe a large population.

translations.source: Àwọn ìlú-ìpinle jẹ àwọn ìsáájú fún àwọn orílè-èdè. Àsà tí ọ̀làjù túnmò sí ìfìoyẹ lẹ́lẹ̀ kọjá ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìran, nípasẹ̀ àsà asájú àti ìtànkálẹ̀ ìtẹ̀lẹ́ra.
translations.reference: City-states are the precursors of nations. A civilizational culture implies the passing on of knowledge across several generations, a lingering cultural footprint and fair dissemination.
translations.hypothesis: State capitals serve as gateways for countries. Traditions that have been passed down through generations, through customs and cultural heritage, are often showcased in these cities.

translations.source: Àwọn àṣà kéèké ma ń pòórá lá ì fi ìtàn kankan sílẹ̀ bí ẹ̀rí, wọn kì í si ri í lò gẹ́gẹ́ bí ohun ìlàjú tó yẹ.
translations.reference: Minor cultures often vanish without leaving relevant historic evidence and fail to be recognized as proper civilizations.
translations.hypothesis: Small traditions often get lost in the telling of a story, and they are not always seen as the important aspects they truly are.

translations.source: Lákòókò ogun àláyìípadà, àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ mẹ́tàlá sèdàsílẹ̀ ìjọba tí kò lágbára—pẹ̀lú níní ìgbìmọ̀ asòfin bí i ẹka kan lábẹ́ àkọọ́lẹ̀ gbogbogbo.
translations.reference: During the Revolutionary War, the thirteen states first formed a weak central government—with the Congress being its only component—under the Articles of Confederation.
translations.hypothesis: During the period of military rule, three states were created by the government—with one of the legislative bodies being a single chamber under a general assembly.

translations.source: Àwọn aṣòfin kò ní agbára láti kan owó orí nípá àti pé kò sí ìgbìmọ̀ aláṣẹ tàbí ìdàjọ́, ó wà lọ́wọ́ àwọn aláṣẹ́ ìpínlẹ̀ tí wọ́n kì í sábàá fọwọ́ṣowọ́pọ̀ láti se àgbéró àwọn òfin gbogbo.
translations.reference: Congress lacked any power to impose taxes, and, because there was no national executive or judiciary, it relied on state authorities, who were often uncooperative, to enforce all its acts.
translations.hypothesis: The laws do not grant the power to arbitrarily seize property or impose taxes, and there is no established system of governance or justice. This situation is common in areas where state authorities are weak and unable to effectively enforce laws and regulations.

translations.source: Kò ní áṣẹ kankan láti mún òfin owó orí àti ìlànà ìdíyelé láàrin ìpínlẹ̀.
translations.reference: It also had no authority to override tax laws and tariffs between states.
translations.hypothesis: There should be no discrimination based on gender or any other form of prejudice within the state.

translations.source: Àkọọ́lẹ̀ tìí bèèrè fún àjùmọgbà ìjẹho látọ̀dọ̀ àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ kí wọ́n tó lè sàtúnse sí i, àmọ́ àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ fọwọ́ yẹpẹrẹ mún ààrin gbungbun ìjọba débi wípé àwọn asojú kì í sí níjoòkó.
translations.reference: The Articles required unanimous consent from all the states before they could be amended and states took the central government so lightly that their representatives were often absent.
translations.hypothesis: The government is seeking feedback from state governments to help refine the policy, but some state officials have expressed concerns about the potential financial burden it could place on their budgets, especially in the absence of adequate funding.

translations.source: Egbe agbaboolu ilu Itili pelu ti Jamani ni egbe agbaboolu keji to se aseyori ju laye, awon de lo gbe igba oroke ni Ere Idije FIFA Koopu Agbaye ni 2006.
translations.reference: Italy's national football, along with German national football team is the second most successful team in the world and were the FIFA World Cup champions in 2006.
translations.hypothesis: The Italian national football team, along with the German national team, is considered one of the most successful teams in the world, having reached the final of the 2006 FIFA World Cup.

translations.source: Àwọn eré ìdárayá tó gbajúmọ̀ ní bọ́ọ̀lù àfẹsẹ̀gbá, bọ́ọ̀lú aláwọ̀n, volley ball, water polo àti eré sísá pẹ̀lú mọ́tò F1.
translations.reference: Popular sports include football, basketball, volleyball, water-polo, fencing, rugby, cycling, ice hockey, roller hockey and F1 motor racing.
translations.hypothesis: Popular sports that involve strategy include soccer, basketball, volleyball, water polo, and Formula 1 racing.

translations.source: Èré ìdárayá ìgbà òtútù ní wọ́n sábàá ma ń se ní ẹkùn àríwá pẹ̀lú àwọn ará ilẹ̀ Italy tó ma ń figagbága nínú ìdíje àgbáyé àti ètò Olympi.
translations.reference: Winter sports are most popular in the Northern regions, with Italians competing in international games and Olympic events.
translations.hypothesis: Fair play and sportsmanship are often demonstrated in the northern region, particularly among Italian athletes who frequently participate in international competitions and the Olympics.

translations.source: Ilẹ̀ Japan ní erékùsù tó tó ẹgbẹ̀rún méje (èyí tó tóbi jù ní Honshu), sọ ilẹ̀ Japan di erékùsù tó tóbi jù sìkeje ní àgbáyé!
translations.reference: Japans holds nearly 7,000 islands (the biggest being Honshu), making Japan the 7th largest island in the world!
translations.hypothesis: Japan has seven main islands, with Honshu being the largest. This makes Japan the second-largest island country in the world!

translations.source: Torí àkókọpọ̀ irékusú tí Japaani ní a máa n sába pe ní “akipelago” nípasẹ̀ ìmọ̀ àyíká.
translations.reference: Due to the cluster/group of islands Japan has, Japan is often referred to, on a geographical stance, as an "archipelago"
translations.hypothesis: The group of islands that Japan is known for is called an "archipelago" in geography.

translations.source: Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ Taiwan ní 15th century níbi tí àwọn awakọ̀ ojú omi Europe gbà kọjà ṣàkọsílẹ̀ orúkọ island na gẹ́gẹ́ bí IIha Formosa, tàbí island tó rẹwà.
translations.reference: Taiwan beginning start way back in 15th century where European sailors passing by record the island’s name as Ilha Formosa, or beautiful island.
translations.hypothesis: Taiwan's history began in the 15th century when European sailors crossed the seas and gave the island its first known name, "Ilha Formosa," which means "beautiful island."

translations.source: Ní ọdún 1624, ilé-iṣẹ́ Dutch East ní ilẹ̀ India se àgbékalẹ̀ ibùdó ní gúúsù ìwọ̀ oòrùn Taiwan, èyí tó mún ìyàtọ̀ bá iṣẹ́ ọ̀gbìn àgbàdo tí àwọn ọmọ onílẹ̀ ń se, tí ó sì tún fààyè sílẹ̀ fún gbígba àwọn òsìṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ China láti síṣẹ́ lórí okò ìrẹsì àti ṣúgà.
translations.reference: In 1624,Dutch East India Company establishes a base in southwestern Taiwan, initiating a transformation in aboriginal grain production practices and employing Chinese laborers to work on its rice and sugar plantations.
translations.hypothesis: In 1624, a Dutch East India Company trading post was established on the southwestern coast of Taiwan. This disrupted the traditional farming practices of the local people and led to the recruitment of Chinese laborers to work in the sugar and salt industries.

translations.source: Ní ọdún 1683, àwọn ọmọ ogun ìran Qing (1644-1912) gba àkóso agbègbèTaiwan western àti northern coastal wọ́n sì sọ Taiwan dí ìlú ti Qing Empire ní 1885.
translations.reference: In 1683, Qing dynasty (1644-1912) forces take control of Taiwan’s western and northern coastal areas and declared Taiwan as a province of the Qing Empire in 1885.
translations.hypothesis: In the year 1683, the Qing dynasty's (1644-1912) military forces took control of western and northern Taiwan, and in 1885, Taiwan was formally declared a province of the Qing Empire.

translations.source: Lọ́dún 1895, lẹ́yìn ìparun ogun Sino àti Japan (1894-1895), ìjọba Qing buwọ́lu àjùmọgbà àláfíà Shimonoseki, nínú èyí tí ó ti gbé agbára kọja Taiwan fún Japan, èyí tó ń darí erékùsù títí dí odún 1945.
translations.reference: In 1895, after defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, by which it cedes sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which rules the island until 1945.
translations.hypothesis: In 1895, following the Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government, through the Treaty of Shimonoseki, ceded Taiwan to Japan. This marked the beginning of Japanese rule over the island, which lasted until 1945.

translations.source: Machu Picchu ní ẹ̀yà mẹ́ta, tó jẹ́ Intihuatana, Te Temple of the Sun, àti Room of the Three Windows.
translations.reference: Machu Picchu consist of three main structures, namely Intihuatana, the Temple of the Sun, and the Room of the Three Windows.
translations.hypothesis: Machu Picchu has three notable features: Intihuatana, the Temple of the Sun, and the Room of the Three Windows.

translations.source: Wọ́n ti se àtúnkọ́ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ilé tó wà létí ilé ńlá, lójúnà àti fún àwọn onírìn afẹ́ ní òye bí wọ́n se rí gẹ́lẹ́.
translations.reference: Most of the buildings on the edges of the complex have been rebuilt in order to give tourists a better idea of how they originally appeared.
translations.hypothesis: They have renovated many of the smaller buildings around the main house, and have added windows to allow visitors a better view.

translations.source: Ní 1976, ìda ọgbọ̀n ti Machu Picchu tí ní ìdápadà ó sì tẹ̀síwájú títí di òní.
translations.reference: By 1976, thirty percent of Machu Picchu had been restored and restoration continues till today.
translations.hypothesis: In 1976, the archaeological site of Machu Picchu was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site and has continued to be a site of ongoing research.

translations.source: Fún àpẹrẹ, ìlànà àwòrán tó pọ̀jù láyé ní 35mm, èyí tó jẹ́ ìwọ̀n fíìmùn tó pọ̀jù níbí fíìmù àtijọ́ se ń lọ.
translations.reference: For example, the most common still image photography format in the world is 35mm, which was the dominant film size at the close of the analog film era.
translations.hypothesis: For example, the most popular film format in the world was 35mm, which was the standard format used in the early days of filmmaking.

translations.source: Wan ṣì ma ń gbe jáde lónìí,ṣùgbọ́n ní pàtàkì abala ìpín rẹ ti jẹ́ ti ìgúnrégé sensor àwòrán kémẹ́rà onídígítà.
translations.reference: It is still produced today, but more importantly its aspect ratio has been inherited by digital camera image sensor formats.
translations.hypothesis: Today, I'm releasing a new feature, but a critical part of it involves the image sensor of the digital camera.

translations.source: Ìwọ̀n ní ààrùndínlógójì mm jẹ, èyí tó dojúrú bákan, ìwọ̀n èèríndínlógójì mm, ní fífè ní mẹ̀rìnlẹ́lógún mm ní gíga.
translations.reference: The 35mm format is actually, somewhat confusingly, 36mm in width by 24mm in height.
translations.hypothesis: The diameter of the screw is 6 mm, with a thread pitch of 1 mm and a length of 16 mm.

translations.source: Abala ìpín fọ́màtì yìí (pínpín pẹ̀lú méjìlá láti lè ní odidi nọ́ḿbà onípínpín) ni a ma ní ó jẹ́ 3:2.
translations.reference: The aspect ratio of this format (dividing by twelve to obtain the simplest whole-number ratio) is therefore said to be 3:2.
translations.hypothesis: The typical ratio for this format (specifically, the ratio with two numbers) is usually 3:2.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ìgúnrégé (ìgúnrégé ebí APS, fún àpẹrẹ) dọ́gba sí tàbí súmọ ìpín náà.
translations.reference: Many common formats (APS family of formats, for example) are equal to or closely approximate this aspect ratio.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the suggestions (such as those from APS, for example) were accepted or approved.

translations.source: Òfin ìkẹta tí wọ́n ma ń bẹnu àtẹ́ lù jùlọ ní ó jẹ́ àlàkalẹ̀ láti se àgbékalẹ̀ ìyàtọ̀ nígbà tí wọ́n ń sàrídájú ìlànà àwòrán.
translations.reference: The much-abused and often-ridiculed rule of thirds is a simple guideline creating dynamism while keeping a measure of order in an image.
translations.hypothesis: The third most common error is the failure to properly distinguish between different image formats.
